messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] sev2 allocator fragmentation detected on run-342-usw2a — persistent growth in reserved pages, multiple container restarts in last 30m :rotating_light:
maya (oncall): ack. I'm on it, triaging now. grabbing logs from the affected pod set.
maya (oncall): short summary: nodes show rising Rss and Cuda OOMs in the runtime pods, container crashlooping 1->3 times per node. suspect paged-attention allocator + KV cache fragmentation.
raj (runtime): can you paste the kernel OOM lines / cuda error snippet? also which model family?
maya (oncall): model family: open-13b-qa-optimized. GPU: a100-40gb. snippet: ```2026-03-17T02:15:41Z runtime[pid=4567]: cudaMemcpyAsync failed: out of memory (err 2)
2026-03-17T02:15:42Z runtime[pid=4567]: allocator: failed to allocate page slab (requested 12MB)
2026-03-17T02:16:03Z container: exit code 137 (OOM)```
lucy (sre): observed node-level page fragmentation metrics spiking; kvcache resident pages not being reclaimed. looks like slow creep -> fragmentation rather than single-shot leak. :thinking_face:
prod-ops: are any customers impacted? do we need a bridge?
cs-rep: support telemetry shows a small bump in 500s for hosted-api in us-west-2 (~1.2% of requests) starting ~02:10. Dedicated customers on the same AZ seeing elevated latency but no full outages reported yet.
maya (oncall): mitigation plan in order: 1) enable immediate compaction on affected node pool (alloc_compact=1) 2) scale up replacement nodes to shift traffic 3) kick kvcache eviction sweep 4) if still noisy, roll runtime to older kernel patch-1.2.3 which has a paging tweak. executing step 1 now.
maya (oncall): running: ```kubectl patch nodepool run-342-usw2a -p '{"spec":{"alloc_compact":true}}'```
maya (oncall): triggering kvcache sweep job: ```kubectl create job kvcache-sweep-1712349998 --image=redwood/runtime-tools -- /bin/sweep --target run-342 --force```
nate (oncall-next): looping in, will assume next steps after your sweep results. if you want me to start draining nodes, say the word. :eyes:
raj (runtime): FYI the allocator has a known fragmentation mode under repeated prefix allocations for long sequences; there's an experimental slab defrag command in the debug tool. cautious about running in prod but could help if compaction doesn't reduce RSS.
maya (oncall): compaction patch applied to pool. nodes reporting reduced page fragmentation metric within 2m. some pods still OOMing but restart rate dropped from 4/min to ~1/10m.
lucy (sre): adding temp autoscale: +2 nodes in the same AZ to absorb traffic while kvcache stabilizes.
prod-ops: started scaling, new nodes green. routing bumped to healthy nodes.
maya (oncall): kicked slab-defrag on one low-traffic node for test: ```/opt/runtime/bin/slab-defrag --node n-07 --dry-run=false --threshold=0.7``` results: reclaimed ~320MB of fragmented pages, no crashes. planning staggered defrag across 2 nodes.
cs-rep: customer impact update: 500s down to 0.3% post compaction. notified customers in us-west-2 with a short note.
raj (runtime): logs show KV cache buckets with high hole count; will open a follow-up issue for allocator heuristics + proactive defrag. need an eval-run to reproduce with long-context traffic.
maya (oncall): handoff notes for nate: cause = progressive KV-cache/paged-attention allocator fragmentation under long-seq workload for open-13b variant on A100. mitigation applied: alloc_compact=true, kvcache sweep job, staggered slab-defrag, +2 nodes. Current status: service degraded -> recovered, low residual restarts. Customer impact reduced to low levels. recommended follow-ups: automated periodic defrag, improve eviction policy, add metric alert for hole-count ratio.
nate (oncall-next): got it. I'll monitor for 2 hours and schedule a rollback/patch window if restarts creep back up. will also coordinate postmortem. :+1:
lucy (sre): filing incident ticket with logs and timeline. assigning to raj for runtime fix, maya for mitigation notes.
raj (runtime): quick note: there is a small risk defrag could spike temporary CPU and GC pauses; we ran on low-traffic node first and saw only brief spikes. proceed with caution.
maya (oncall): thanks all — marking this thread as on-call-handoff. will post final summary after 1h observation. :white_check_mark:
